notes: CardDemo's sign-on (CC00, COSGN00C) on a GENERATED map input (#4506): 30 scenarios whose COMMAREA is generated and whose RECEIVE MAP input is typed for COSGN0's two unprotected fields, USERID and PASSWD (8 bytes each), over a generated USRSEC file: the id is drawn from the file or misses it, the password is the stored one, a wrong one or empty, and the key pressed turns through ENTER, PF3 and PF7. Proves the carddemo-signon port on inputs it was not written against; the hand-written scenarios left are fault runs, the lowercase fold and the COMMAREA lengths. scenarios.name: first-entry
scenarios.why: #4506: a hand-written scenario of carddemo-signon that the generated inputs do not reach

scenarios.name: lowercase-credentials
scenarios.why: UPPER-CASE on both the id and the password

scenarios.name: admin-xctl-not-authorised
scenarios.why: #4628: NOTAUTH on the admin sign-on's XCTL to COADM01C; COSGN00C has no HANDLE CONDITION / ERROR, so CICS abends the task (AEY7): kills the condition() / XCTL RESP tests of the port

scenarios.name: user-xctl-not-authorised
scenarios.why: #4628: NOTAUTH on the regular user's XCTL to COMEN01C: the same abend on the other XCTL

scenarios.name: user-signs-on-short-commarea
scenarios.why: #4628: the caller passed 100 of the COMMAREA's 160 bytes (EIBCALEN 100, X23): the port cuts DFHCOMMAREA to EIBCALEN and restores the record before writing the task's object back; COSGN00C never references DFHCOMMAREA

scenarios.name: user-file-io-error

faults.why: 17 on the READ -> WHEN OTHER: 'Unable to verify the User ...'

scenarios.why: #4506: a hand-written scenario of carddemo-signon that the generated inputs do not reach

scenarios.name: eibcalen-zero-with-commarea
scenarios.why: #4049: the caller passed a COMMAREA of length 0 (EIBCALEN 0, X23) with ENTER: COSGN00C tests EIBCALEN = 0 first and shows the first-entry screen, not the AID branch (the credentials are not read); the COMMAREA is present, unlike first-entry

scenarios.name: sysid-sent
scenarios.why: SYSIDI arrives with 8 bytes: ASSIGN SYSID writes 4 and the other 4 stay as received (a MOVE would space them, #4049)
